steps.name: MODE
steps.note: DATA-U.

steps.name: AGC
steps.note: AUTO (picks MID in DATA-U). AGC OFF clipped the USB receive audio in two independent tests. The WSJT-X guide's general advice to run AGC off doesn't suit this radio.

steps.name: NR
steps.note: DNR off.

steps.name: ANF
steps.note: DNF off.

steps.name: APF
steps.note: CONTOUR/APF off.

steps.name: DATA MOD SOURCE
steps.note: RADIO SETTING > MODE PSK/DATA > DATA MOD SOURCE = REAR (the rear/USB audio path, not the mic).

steps.name: REAR SELECT
steps.note: RADIO SETTING > MODE PSK/DATA > REAR SELECT = USB. The factory default is DATA (the rear jack), so this must change. EX010416 was read back on a real FT-DX10 (reply EX0104161; on a station running USB audio) [S9].

steps.name: RPORT GAIN
steps.note: Transmit audio gain for the rear input that REAR SELECT picks, including USB (the FT-DX10 has no separate USB MOD GAIN; that's an FTDX101 item). Both USB setup guides tune it. Use 30–70 and keep the computer's output level modest. EX010417 was read back on a real FT-DX10; that test station runs 005, below this range [S9].

steps.name: DATA SHIFT (SSB)
steps.note: Centre of the audio passband, 0000–3000 Hz. 1500 is the factory default.

steps.name: DATA OUT LEVEL
steps.note: Check only. Yaesu's manual describes this as the rear RTTY/DATA jack level, not USB audio; sources run it at 0 or 50. The codes are confirmed; the effect on USB audio is not.

steps.name: TX BPF SEL
steps.note: 400–2600 Hz suits WSJT-X with Split = Fake It. Use 50–3050 (0) with Split = None or for MSK144. Recommended by one author; the factory default is 300–2700. EX010414 was read back on a real FT-DX10 [S9].

steps.name: Receive width

manual.menu: WIDTH (and R.FIL 3 kHz)

steps.note: So the whole 0–3 kHz audio window reaches the computer.

steps.name: CAT RATE

manual.menu: OPERATION SETTING > GENERAL > CAT RATE

steps.note: Change this on the radio, not over CAT (the link drops when the rate changes). Match it in your software.

steps.note: The speech processor is for tough conditions, not normal QSOs (Yaesu). When you do use it, keep the COMP meter at or below 10 dB.
